A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReVeal research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite retitling, reorganization and expanded experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, LiveCodeBench evaluations, reward ablations and training analyses in Table 2 and Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: V2 reports original LiveCodeBench and CodeContests results, training diagnostics, and memory, repeated-experiment and prompt-only comparisons in the main text and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a short-term memory component retaining only the last three turns during inference, with a full-history comparison in Appendix C. The generation-verification loop, test filtering, rewards and credit-assignment equations remain equivalent; renaming TA-PPO to TAPO does not establish a new optimization algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates LiveCodeBench problems from August 2024–January 2025. V2 substantially expands evaluation coverage with CodeContests and LiveCodeBench V6 from February–May 2025, while retaining V5 Qwen evaluations in the appendices. TACO training coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated prompt-only ReVeal comparator without RL training (Table 9) and removes DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B from the reported comparisons. The base models, single-turn RL and Qwen2.5-Coder, GPT-4o and CTRL critic comparators remain.

E3.justification: Reported DAPO evaluation settings change from 51,200 to 32,768 maximum response tokens and from Pass@1 temperature 0.2/0.6 to 0.6 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 3). Main evaluation budgets change from 6/19 to 8/25 turns, and Pass@k switches from Qwen with six turns to DAPO with ten. These are substantial protocol revisions; the training hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends reward ablations to DAPO on both main benchmarks and adds verification-accuracy training curves (Table 1, Figure 4). Appendix C tests truncated versus complete history, while Appendix E compares trained and untrained ReVeal using identical prompts and tools across one, three and six turns. These add substantive controls beyond v1's reward and scaling analyses.

E5.justification: V2 first reports eight repeated experiments and mean ± standard deviation for the Qwen reward comparison: 37.09 ± 0.33 versus 38.02 ± 0.31 (Table 8). V1 reports rollout counts without comparable variability estimates. V2 does not clarify whether training or evaluation is repeated, or specify a formal significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V1's headline 42.4% after 19 turns on older LiveCodeBench is replaced by 38.7% on V6 and 33.6% on CodeContests after 25 turns; these are different-condition results, not a demonstrated performance decline. The retained Qwen outcome-only result changes from 37.5% to 37.1%, critic entries are revised, and new memory, prompt-only, repeated-experiment and DAPO diagnostic results are reported.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, GAE expression, token and turn return recurrences, and advantage construction match after renumbering (v1 Equations 1–9; v2 Equations 1–8). The new verification-generation asymmetry discussion is conceptual, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about joint generation-verification optimization and reasoning beyond the training horizon remain. V2 adds the explicit claim that ReVeal widens verification-generation asymmetry, conditions its general applicability on that asymmetry, and removes the headline claim of surpassing DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B.

C2.justification: V2 adds an asymmetry-based mechanism explanation and discusses how stronger code and tests reinforce each other. It also explains Figure 4's early accuracy dip through expanding format-valid evaluation coverage and qualifies critic comparisons by benchmark period. These refine the retained co-evolution and feedback-guided exploration interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the three-turn memory window and retained interaction contents, clarifies the critic results' source period, and documents format-dependent diagnostic coverage. Evaluation hyperparameter entries are revised. Hardware, training software, TACO preprocessing, prompt and feedback templates, and the promise of future project release remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wei and Setlur for verification asymmetry and test-time scaling, discusses ReAct and Reflexion, and describes ReVeal as complementary to other tool-augmented approaches. It also adds the AlphaCode/CodeContests citation and removes the Qwen technical report and SRPO references. Most prior RL and self-verification positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the methods and analysis are rewritten around reliable self-verification. TA-PPO becomes TAPO, the main narrative focuses on DAPO, and the worked example and Qwen analyses move into a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds the asymmetry schematic, redraws the framework with memory, introduces DAPO diagnostic plots, expands the main table to two benchmarks, and adds uncertainty and prompt-only tables. The worked example and Qwen displays move to the appendices; the Qwen last-turn training plot is extended, and table styling and page layout change extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support by adding CodeContests and newer LiveCodeBench evaluations and a matched prompt/tool control that addresses whether prompting and tool access alone explain the gains. Memory ablation and repeated-experiment variability further improve assessment. These benefits outweigh remaining weaknesses: critic comparisons still mix benchmark periods, and the claimed statistical significance lacks a specified test.
